claims.text: Signed the 24 June 2009 letter to Deputy Secretary of Defense William J. Lynn III, on Senate Majority Leader letterhead, requesting DoD place the AAITP under 'Restricted Special Access Protection'.

claims.nodeLabel: Reid Letter to DEPSECDEF Requesting Restricted SAP Status
claims.text: Text: 'Since the Advanced Aerospace Threat and Identification Program (AAITP) and study were first commissioned, much progress has been made with the identification of several highly sensitive, unconventional aerospace-related findings. Given the current rate of success, the continued study of these subjects will likely lead to technology advancements that in the immediate near-term will require extraordinary protection. Due to the sensitivities of the information surrounding aspects of this program, I require your assistance in establishing a [restricted special access program].'

edges.note: He signed it. The letter of 24 June 2009 to Deputy Secretary William J. Lynn III went on Senate Majority Leader letterhead - 'HARRY REID, MAJORITY LEADER, NEVADA' - and asked the Department to place the programme under a restricted special access programme.

edges.label: Senate Majority Leader in 2009 - in the Gang of Eight, not in the 119(e)(2) group
edges.note: This is the cleanest demonstration that the two small groups are different sets. 50 U.S.C. 3093(c)(2) includes the majority and minority leaders of the Senate. 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) and 119(g) do not; they reach only committee and subcommittee chairs and ranking members. A Senate Majority Leader has no statutory entitlement to waived DoD SAP notification by virtue of that office. In 2009 the Senate armed services and appropriations seats were held by Levin, McCain, Inouye and Cochran.

edges.label: Reid's Nevada base; earmark performed by a Las Vegas constituent
edges.note: This is not merely a home-town link. AARO's official history names 'Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV)' as having directed the appropriation, and the federal award record places Bigelow's company in Nevada; the money Reid secured was performed by a company in the state he represented. Tier 2 because the constituent relationship is the inference joining those two documented facts, not something either document states.
